summary: Horn defended bodily continuity, appearances, sincerity, and the empty tomb, while O'Connor pressed source ambiguity, rival-testimony parity, corroboration deficits, and natural alternatives.

pro.text: That's striking that they proclaim Jesus rose.
pro.context: Horn emphasizes that the earliest proclamation concerned resurrection, not merely heavenly survival or continuing spiritual existence.

con.text: not just being a Christian, not just spreading the message
con.context: O'Connor distinguishes persecution for general Christian affiliation from martyrdom specifically grounded in firsthand bodily-resurrection testimony.

con-bodily-inconsistent-physicality.words: Pauline spiritual language and Gospel reports of barrier crossing sit uneasily beside touching and eating, leaving the appearances ambiguous as evidence for ordinary physical embodiment.
con-bodily-inconsistent-physicality.critique: Strongest feature: The argument carefully juxtaposes Pauline flesh-and-blood language, barrier-crossing capacities, and invitations to touch or observe eating, thereby establishing a coherent textual ambiguity without prematurely asserting metaphysical impossibility. Principal limitation: Its phrase ordinary physical body remains insufficiently specified, because transformed embodiment could preserve corporeal continuity while possessing properties unavailable to mortal organisms, and the relevant sources differ substantially in chronology, genre, and theological purpose. Live burden: The skeptical case must explain why these heterogeneous descriptions collectively undermine physical continuity rather than characterize an extraordinary but embodied transformation, while the affirmative case must reconcile every cited anomaly consistently. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects excellent central relevance, explicit qualification, substantial representational charity, and persuasive internal coherence, moderated by compressed source analysis and an incompletely stabilized physicality criterion.

con-rival-mormon-witness-parity.words: Collective Mormon testimony, continuing attestation after estrangement, persecution, and disputed physical or visionary experiences create a consistency test for evaluating resurrection witnesses.
con-rival-mormon-witness-parity.critique: Strongest feature: The comparison identifies concrete testimonial characteristics, including collective attestation, institutional estrangement, continued affirmation, persecution, and uncertainty about physical versus visionary experience, so the analogy functions as a disciplined consistency test rather than superficial association. Principal limitation: The argument does not independently establish that the traditions share comparable incentives, documentation, temporal proximity, background constraints, or explanatory contexts, and therefore cannot derive evidential equivalence merely from overlapping witness features. Live burden: The resurrection case must demonstrate which disanalogies materially affect reliability, while the skeptical case must show that its transferred criteria remain stable across both traditions and do not selectively discount inconvenient differences. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects exceptional relevance, clarity, calibration, and comparative coherence, with modest restraint for compressed historical substantiation and unresolved differences between the underlying testimonial environments.

con-five-hundred-corroboration-limits.words: Brigham Young transfiguration reports provide more identifiable testimonial detail than Paul's five-hundred claim, whose witnesses, circumstances, beliefs, accessibility, and independence remain unknown.
con-five-hundred-corroboration-limits.critique: Strongest feature: The move converts a generalized complaint about evidence into specific verification questions concerning witness identities, gathering circumstances, accessibility, prior beliefs, independence, and documentary survival, thereby making the corroboration deficit unusually concrete and historically relevant. Principal limitation: Greater surviving detail in the Brigham Young tradition does not automatically establish greater overall reliability, since chronology, transmission, social coordination, theological expectation, and alternative explanations also require symmetrical evaluation. Live burden: The affirmative case must explain what evidential work Paul's early report can perform without identifiable witnesses, while the skeptical comparison must demonstrate that its better-documented analogue remains sufficiently comparable beyond possessing additional names and dates. Locked score: The very strong performance band recognizes excellent precision, coherent comparative pressure, and direct contact with corroboration, while preserving a measured deduction for the somewhat overstated inference from relative detail to comparative evidential superiority.

pro-bodily-pauline-physicality.words: Paul's Jewish resurrection framework and transformed-body language support corporeality, while eating, denial of ghostliness, and an empty tomb distinguish resurrection from disembodied survival.
pro-bodily-pauline-physicality.critique: Strongest feature: The reply integrates Jewish resurrection expectations, Pauline transformed-body language, embodied Gospel conduct, explicit denial of ghostliness, and the empty tomb into a unified interpretation of corporeal continuity rather than merely disembodied survival. Principal limitation: Although this synthesis directly addresses the main ambiguity objection, it leaves barrier crossing and untouchability comparatively underexplained and treats disputed Pauline terminology with greater confidence than the acknowledged interpretive alternatives warrant. Live burden: The affirmative case must show that extraordinary transformed capacities coexist consistently with physical identity across the relevant sources, while the skeptical case must explain why Jewish context and embodied narrative details fail to shift the balance toward corporeality. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects comprehensive responsiveness, exceptional burden relevance, stable terminology, and charitable engagement, moderated only by residual semantic uncertainty and incomplete reconciliation of every Gospel anomaly.

pro-rivals-supernatural-admissibility.words: Christian theology may admit genuine wonders among non-Christians without treating an isolated divine intervention as endorsement of every surrounding doctrine or institution.
pro-rivals-supernatural-admissibility.critique: Strongest feature: The argument draws a precise and logically valuable distinction between acknowledging an extraordinary event and endorsing the complete doctrinal system associated with its beneficiary, while limiting itself appropriately to theological possibility. Principal limitation: This admissibility distinction does not evaluate the reliability, independence, incentives, or physical character of Mormon testimony and therefore leaves the central comparative-evidence challenge substantially untouched despite offering relevant background clarification. Live burden: The affirmative case must connect permissive supernatural theology to consistent historical discrimination among competing reports, whereas the skeptical case must avoid treating acknowledgment of a possible rival wonder as wholesale validation of its religious interpretation. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects outstanding conceptual coherence, careful qualification, and considerable subsidiary relevance, balanced against low direct responsiveness to testimonial parity and an evidential warrant that remains principally theological rather than historical.

pro-rivals-mormon-differences.words: Mormon claims differ through witness prompting, prior investment, Joseph Smith's incentives, possible artifacts or hoaxes, internal discrepancies, and conflict with established historical knowledge.
pro-rivals-mormon-differences.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies several potentially reliability-relevant disanalogies, including prompting, prior investment, worldly incentives, possible artifacts, documented hoaxes, discrepancies, and conflicts with established background knowledge, rather than dismissing the comparison categorically. Principal limitation: It moves among Joseph Smith, different witness groups, plates, angelic encounters, and broader historical claims without consistently specifying which objection bears on which testimony, and it does not squarely answer continued attestation after institutional estrangement. Live burden: The affirmative case must disaggregate these differences and demonstrate their comparative magnitude under one stable evidential framework, while the skeptical case must show that estranged testimony survives those targeted objections. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects meaningful central contact, numerous concrete distinctions, and generally coherent discrimination, restrained by incomplete scope control, underdeveloped comparative weighting, and an important unanswered independence consideration.

con-paul-gospel-development.words: Paul remains unclear about resurrection physicality, while later Gospel appearances become increasingly elaborate and theological rather than independently resolving the earliest ambiguity.
con-paul-gospel-development.critique: Strongest feature: The reply sharply distinguishes Paul's earlier, comparatively ambiguous terminology from later Gospel elaboration and directly challenges the claim that transformed-body language already supplies an unambiguous description of physical continuity. Principal limitation: The developmental inference receives limited historical demonstration, because increasing narrative detail can reflect preserved embodied traditions, authorial selection, or theological exposition without necessarily representing fabrication or progressive materialization. Live burden: The skeptical case must substantiate the direction and mechanism of development across sources, while the affirmative case must establish why later embodied scenes preserve independent early memory rather than simply interpret earlier proclamation. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects direct and comprehensive responsiveness, precise qualification, high central relevance, and charitable representation of the opposing interpretation, with a measured reservation for compressed source-critical evidence supporting the proposed developmental trajectory.

pro-bodily-continuity-wounds.words: Pauline bodily terminology indicates corporeality, and Jesus's retained crucifixion wounds identify the risen figure as the same embodied person who underwent crucifixion.
pro-bodily-continuity-wounds.critique: Strongest feature: The retained-wounds argument gives the bodily-continuity claim a vivid identity criterion, explaining why the narratives portray the risen figure as the same crucified person rather than a duplicate, apparition, or unrelated spiritual entity. Principal limitation: Its historical force depends upon the reliability and antiquity of the wound narratives, and the move neither establishes those prerequisites nor reconciles retained injuries with the barrier-crossing and untouchable characteristics emphasized by the skeptical challenge. Live burden: The affirmative case must demonstrate that the motif preserves early experiential testimony rather than later literary identification, while the skeptical case must explain why narrative continuity contributes no meaningful evidence even conditionally. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects excellent coherence, unmistakable central relevance, and persuasive conditional reasoning, moderated by incomplete responsiveness, implicit source assumptions, and slightly overstated confidence in historical application.

pro-appearances-group-source.words: Luke's reliability and relationship with Paul support group-appearance reports, while the limited appearance period weighs against indefinitely expanding visionary enthusiasm.
pro-appearances-group-source.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a recognizable historical route from Luke's relationship with Paul and narrative competence to group-appearance testimony, then adds the finite appearance period as a constraint upon uncontrolled visionary proliferation. Principal limitation: General source reliability and association with Paul do not establish identifiable witness independence, direct access, or event verification, and the response never supplies the requested particulars concerning the five hundred or adequately excludes visionary transmission. Live burden: The affirmative case must specify Luke's evidential access and distinguish faithful reporting of tradition from independent corroboration, while the skeptical case must assess whether bounded appearances nonetheless carry cumulative explanatory weight. Locked score: The mixed performance band reflects genuine relevance, clear presentation, and partial contact with source development, offset by materially overstated warrant, broad reliability language, incomplete verification, and failure to answer the narrow corroboration demand.

pro-sincerity-informed-danger.words: Danger confronted by informed apostolic proclaimers supports sincerity, while Paul's conversion from hostile persecutor supplies an incentive-relevant difference from the proposed Mormon parallel.
pro-sincerity-informed-danger.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly limits danger to evidence of sincerity rather than truth and identifies Paul's hostile prior commitment as a potentially important comparative difference unavailable in the specific Mormon parallel under discussion. Principal limitation: It shifts between apostles generally and Paul individually without establishing which proclaimers possessed firsthand bodily information, what dangers each confronted, or how continued Mormon attestation after estrangement should affect the comparative incentive analysis. Live burden: The affirmative case must connect specified knowledge to specified costs for identifiable witnesses, while the skeptical case must acknowledge that prior hostility and costly conversion can increase sincerity without establishing physical resurrection. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects a coherent, explicitly qualified sincerity inference and meaningful comparative contact, tempered by incomplete historical specification, unanswered estranged testimony, uncertain witness knowledge, and modest overstatement of the available evidence.

pro-sincerity-apostolic-risk.words: Early apostolic danger supports sincere resurrection proclamation without independently proving resurrection, and apocryphal reports require individual assessment rather than wholesale acceptance or rejection.
pro-sincerity-apostolic-risk.critique: Strongest feature: The move carefully distinguishes sincere proclamation from demonstrated resurrection and advocates case-by-case evaluation of apocryphal material, thereby avoiding both wholesale acceptance and indiscriminate dismissal of heterogeneous early reports. Principal limitation: It does not resolve the principal bodily-source challenge available in the exchange and leaves substantially assumed which apostles possessed firsthand information, which dangers are historically early, and whether any death resulted specifically from resurrection testimony. Live burden: The affirmative case must join individualized source assessment to identifiable knowledge and consequences, while the skeptical case must distinguish incomplete documentation from positive evidence that sincere proclamation lacked firsthand grounding. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects commendable calibration, conceptual clarity, and relevant sincerity support, balanced against partial responsiveness, underdeveloped historical particulars, and an evidential bridge from general apostolic danger to informed bodily testimony that remains incomplete.

pro-tomb-sober-women.words: Canonical tomb narratives appear restrained beside later embellishments, while guards and socially disadvantageous women witnesses support an early historical empty-tomb tradition.
pro-tomb-sober-women.critique: Strongest feature: The reply answers narrative-development concerns through a concrete contrast between comparatively restrained canonical accounts and later embellishment, while identifying women witnesses and guard traditions as potentially counterproductive or explanatory details. Principal limitation: Sobriety and social disadvantage require historically specific benchmarks, and apologetic usefulness can itself explain these narrative features, so their presence does not independently establish every burial, guard, or discovery detail as historical. Live burden: The affirmative case must demonstrate why these features are better predicted by early remembered discovery than by literary or apologetic construction, while the skeptical case must explain their cumulative evidential significance rather than dismissing them individually. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects direct responsiveness, coherent authenticity indicators, and substantial central relevance, moderated by contextual assumptions, limited independent corroboration, and an inference from narrative characteristics to historical emptiness that remains somewhat overstated.

con-postmortem-extrabiblical-gap.words: Jesus's pre-crucifixion life receives supportive and hostile extrabiblical corroboration, whereas reported postmortem appearances, including the five hundred, lack comparable independent confirmation.
con-postmortem-extrabiblical-gap.critique: Strongest feature: The reply draws a clean temporal and evidential distinction between external corroboration for Jesus's pre-crucifixion existence and activity and the absence of comparable independent confirmation for reported postmortem encounters. Principal limitation: Saying that extrabiblical material is absent compresses disputes about later non-Christian references, source dependence, expected documentary survival, and whether hostile silence should carry substantial weight in the relevant ancient evidential environment. Live burden: The affirmative case must explain why early Christian reports remain historically weighty without external confirmation, while the skeptical case must specify what corroboration should reasonably have survived and how its absence changes comparative probability. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects exceptional responsiveness, precision, relevance, and disciplined focus upon the five-hundred claim, with limited restraint for compressed expectations about surviving evidence and the categorical phrasing of the extrabiblical deficit.

pro-appearances-conversions-conduct.words: Resurrection unifies James's movement from unbelief, Paul's conversion from persecution, and the apostles' reported transition from fear to bold public proclamation.
pro-appearances-conversions-conduct.critique: Strongest feature: The argument assembles James's prior unbelief, Paul's hostility, and the apostles' reported behavioral transformation into a concise explanatory pattern that a resurrection hypothesis can address through one overarching causal account. Principal limitation: It does not provide the requested independent corroboration, leaves source dependence and alternative psychological explanations implicit, and asserts that competing accounts are considerably harder without conducting a sufficiently discriminating comparison among them. Live burden: The affirmative case must establish the underlying conversion and conduct data independently and compare resurrection against specific alternatives, while the skeptical case must explain the convergent pattern without trivializing sincere transformative experiences. Locked score: The mixed performance band reflects clear explanatory relevance and a potentially valuable cumulative inference, counterbalanced by nonresponsiveness to corroboration, underdeveloped comparative analysis, uncertain evidential independence, and stronger confidence than the presented warrant supports.

con-martyrdom-bodily-knowledge-gap.words: Persecution and martyrdom cannot establish bodily resurrection when clear cases concern visions or leave uncertain what alleged witnesses experienced and why they died.
con-martyrdom-bodily-knowledge-gap.critique: Strongest feature: The diagnostic precisely separates suffering, sincerity, firsthand bodily experience, and the particular reason for persecution or death, preventing evidence for commitment from silently becoming evidence for physical resurrection. Principal limitation: The move compresses the completeness of the historical record and could more fully assess whether several individually incomplete indicators nevertheless provide cumulative support for informed apostolic conviction beyond Paul's visionary description. Live burden: The affirmative case must identify witnesses who both encountered the bodily figure and suffered specifically for maintaining that testimony, while the skeptical case must distinguish evidential insufficiency from claims that no relevant connection existed. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects exceptional conceptual precision, comprehensive diagnostic responsiveness, careful calibration, and direct contact with the central sincerity gap, with only modest reservation for abbreviated treatment of cumulative evidence and source completeness.

con-reburial-theft-alternatives.words: Emergency Sabbath burial followed by proper reburial, or alternatively grave robbery, supplies historically possible explanations for an empty tomb without uniquely indicating resurrection.
con-reburial-theft-alternatives.critique: Strongest feature: The reply grants the reported discovery conditionally and then supplies separately identifiable natural mechanisms, including temporary emergency placement, subsequent reburial, and grave robbery, without overclaiming that any single hypothesis has been established. Principal limitation: The alternatives remain possibilities rather than developed comparative explanations, and the move does not quantify their fit with honorable burial, preserved goods, later proclamation, appearance traditions, or the practical knowledge of those associated with the tomb. Live burden: The skeptical case must connect at least one mechanism to the wider evidence without accumulating unsupported auxiliary assumptions, while the affirmative case must show why each historically possible route fits materially worse than resurrection. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects exemplary calibration, direct responsiveness, high central relevance, and substantial historical plausibility, tempered by incomplete integration with appearance evidence and limited comparative detail.

pro-tomb-alternatives-conjunction.words: Natural accounts require combined missing-body and appearance mechanisms, while grave robbery fits poorly with preserved burial goods and removal of an intact corpse.
pro-tomb-alternatives-conjunction.critique: Strongest feature: The reply recognizes that a complete natural explanation must address both missing-body and appearance evidence and adds a concrete objection that ordinary grave robbery more naturally targets valuables than removal of an intact body. Principal limitation: A conjunction receives a serious probability penalty only after dependence, background plausibility, and evidential fit are assessed, while the resurrection explanation also contains substantive commitments that cannot be exempted from symmetrical comparison. Live burden: The affirmative case must model why the proposed natural mechanisms are sufficiently independent and cumulatively strained, while the skeptical case must present an integrated alternative rather than an expandable menu of disconnected possibilities. Locked score: The strong performance band reflects direct contact with tomb alternatives, clear comparative structure, and useful attention to robbery incentives, moderated by incomplete testimonial engagement, implicit dependence assumptions, and somewhat overstated probabilistic consequences.

con-pilate-burial-plausibility.words: The Gospel portrayal of Pilate compassionately permitting Jesus's burial is historically questionable because other accounts characterize him as an exceptionally ruthless provincial ruler.
con-pilate-burial-plausibility.critique: Strongest feature: The reply tests a prerequisite of the tomb narrative against external character evidence, usefully asking whether the Gospel portrayal of Pilate coheres with descriptions of his broader ruthlessness and administrative conduct. Principal limitation: Ruthlessness does not exclude pragmatic burial authorization, accommodation of local pressure, or indifference to corpse disposition, and the move neither identifies the comparative sources nor establishes that compassion was necessary for the reported permission. Live burden: The skeptical case must connect Pilate's documented governance to burial practice in this circumstance, while the affirmative case must explain authorization without relying upon an implausibly benevolent characterization. Locked score: The mixed performance band reflects genuine subsidiary relevance and direct contact with burial plausibility, offset by weak evidential specification, a questionable character-to-action inference, limited charity toward pragmatic alternatives, and failure to address the conjunction or robbery reasoning itself.

con-defection-testimony-independence.words: Retaining an extraordinary-experience claim while repudiating its associated institution can reduce a simple loyalty explanation and increase testimonial independence rather than weaken it.
con-defection-testimony-independence.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly reverses the incentive inference about estranged witnesses and explains why repudiating an institution while preserving an originating experience can reduce simple explanations based upon loyalty, authority, or continuing institutional reward. Principal limitation: Defection does not eliminate prior commitment, face-saving, social relationships, memory reconstruction, or selective retention, so increased independence is a conditional consideration rather than a general guarantee of testimonial reliability. Live burden: The skeptical case must establish the circumstances and continuing incentives of particular witnesses, while the affirmative case must show why prompting, artifacts, or historical conflicts outweigh the independence gained through institutional repudiation. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects exceptionally direct responsiveness, careful conditional phrasing, coherent incentive analysis, and central comparative relevance, with measured restraint because the empirical details behind the generalized defector model remain comparatively compressed.

con-firsthand-specific-martyrdom-deficit.words: The record lacks combined evidence of identifiable firsthand bodily encounters and martyrdom specifically for that resurrection testimony rather than for Christian affiliation generally.
con-firsthand-specific-martyrdom-deficit.critique: Strongest feature: The response formulates the exact missing evidential conjunction: identifiable firsthand experience of the bodily risen Jesus together with credible persecution or death specifically attributable to maintaining that particular testimony. Principal limitation: Its diagnosis depends upon the completeness and interpretation of the historical record discussed, and it could more fully evaluate whether early proclamation, general persecution, and multiple incomplete traditions jointly support informed conviction despite absent testimony-specific death documentation. Live burden: The affirmative case must provide person-specific links among bodily knowledge, proclamation, danger, and cause of death, while the skeptical case must preserve the distinction between an evidential deficit and categorical historical denial. Locked score: The very strong performance band reflects outstanding precision, comprehensive responsiveness across several opposing moves, careful calibration, exceptional charity, and decisive central relevance, with only limited reservation for compressed assessment of cumulative indirect evidence.

strengths: Connected Jewish resurrection expectations, Pauline transformed-body language, embodied encounters, and the empty tomb into a coherent physical-continuity interpretation.
Distinguished sincerity from truth and repeatedly treated danger or martyrdom as supporting commitment rather than independently proving resurrection.
Offered concrete differences between Mormon and resurrection traditions, including prompting, incentives, artifacts, historical background, and Paul's prior hostility.
Challenged natural explanations to account jointly for missing-body and appearance evidence instead of addressing each datum in isolation.

blunders.text: The group-appearance defense relied on broad confidence in Luke without supplying identifiable, independent corroboration for the five hundred.
The rival-miracle response did not adequately address continued Mormon attestation after estrangement or consistently match each proposed disanalogy to a particular claim.
The martyrdom case left person-specific links among firsthand bodily knowledge, danger, and testimony-specific death substantially underdeveloped.
The conjunction argument assumed a probability penalty without sufficiently examining dependence among natural mechanisms or equivalent commitments within the resurrection hypothesis.

strengths: Separated mixed Pauline and Gospel descriptions from an unambiguous claim of ordinary physical embodiment while acknowledging evidence in both directions.
Converted the five-hundred report into specific verification questions about identity, accessibility, independence, beliefs, and gathering circumstances.
Applied a detailed rival-testimony consistency test and directly explained why institutional defection can increase witness independence.
Distinguished sincere suffering from firsthand bodily knowledge and from martyrdom specifically caused by resurrection testimony.
Presented reburial and theft as calibrated historical possibilities rather than claiming that either alternative was established.

blunders.text: The comparison with better-documented Mormon reports sometimes moved too quickly from greater surviving detail to stronger overall evidential standing.
The Gospel-development claim remained historically compressed and did not fully establish why later physical details represent elaboration rather than preserved tradition.
The Pilate objection treated general ruthlessness as stronger evidence against pragmatic burial authorization than the presented warrant supported.
The natural tomb alternatives were not fully integrated with the appearance and proclamation evidence into a single developed historical account.

newArguments.title: Comparative Explanatory Compression
newArguments.text: A stronger cumulative case would compare how many independently motivated assumptions each explanation requires across bodily proclamation, reported appearances, conversion, conduct, and the tomb tradition. Resurrection should not receive a free pass merely because it is a single label, but neither should several natural mechanisms be counted as one explanation without examining their coordination. The relevant question is comparative compression: which account explains the greatest range of data with the fewest unsupported auxiliary commitments, given each participant's background assumptions about supernatural possibility?

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit explanatory-compression framework not articulated as such in any locked participant move.

newArguments.title: Constraint from Early Claim Content
newArguments.text: The evidential significance of early proclamation depends not merely on its date but on its content. If the earliest recoverable claim already concerned the crucified Jesus's resurrection rather than generic heavenly vindication, later bodily narratives may elaborate an existing corporeal core instead of creating it wholesale. This argument requires careful linguistic and source analysis and does not establish every Gospel detail, but it gives the affirmative case a principled way to resist a simple progression from vision to physicality while acknowledging development in narrative presentation.

newArguments.title: Evidence-Type Separation
newArguments.text: A disciplined skeptical account should separate evidence into claim formation, witness sincerity, bodily specificity, and corpse location. Early proclamation may strongly support early belief; conversion and danger may support sincerity; Gospel scenes may support later bodily interpretation; and tomb traditions may support some missing-body claim. None of those evidential categories automatically transfers its strength to the others. This separation prevents a cumulative argument from gaining apparent force through repeated counting of dependent traditions and clarifies exactly where additional independent evidence would be needed.

newArguments.title: Expected Corroboration Calibration
newArguments.text: The absence of independent postmortem corroboration matters only relative to what the historical circumstances make reasonable to expect. A stronger skeptical case would identify which alleged appearances were public enough, socially consequential enough, or connected to accessible witnesses strongly enough that additional testimony or hostile engagement might plausibly survive. This avoids treating ancient documentary silence as automatically decisive while still distinguishing a named report from independently recoverable witness evidence. The method strengthens the corroboration objection through calibrated expectations rather than a categorical appeal to missing records.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed treatment of documentary silence by supplying an explicit expectation-sensitive standard.
